Your values have to show up.
Only Empowerment is the free educational companion to The PERIOD Code by Jim Lunsford. Learn its six connected values through full lessons and practical examples.
Knowing what matters is a start. The work is putting it into action.
Start with an ordinary moment
You owe someone an update.
You promised an update. The work is running late, and you want to avoid the conversation.
Before you read on, notice what you're waiting for.
The negotiation
“I’ll send an update once I have better news.”
The message keeps moving further away because telling the truth feels uncomfortable.
The standard
“When a deadline is at risk, I send an honest update before it passes.”
You cannot guarantee the result. You can communicate what is true, what is delayed, and what you can realistically do next.
What you can own
Send the honest update before the deadline. Say what is finished, what is delayed, and what you can realistically do next.
Ownership puts the responsibility for that response with you. Integrity keeps the update truthful. Discipline means following through.
A value becomes visible in behavior.
A value tells you what matters. A standard gives that value a line to live by. Sending the update is the action that makes it visible.
Understanding this example is a start. Your behavior supplies the evidence.
What if the plan really needs to change?

New information, limited capacity, or safety can require a different plan. Tell the truth about the change and choose a workable response. Holding a value does not require protecting a method that causes harm.
Put it beside your own day.
What responsibility are you waiting to feel ready for?
Name it privately. Then name one action you can take without waiting for someone else to change. It might be a correction, a boundary, or a request for help.
You are responsible for your response, not another person's harmful actions. Getting help can be part of taking ownership.
Why PERIOD?
PERIOD marks the end of the old negotiation. You stop making responsibility wait for a better mood or an easier day. You act on a standard, and return to it when you fall short.
The Code is a connected standard for living. One action gives you somewhere to begin; all six values continue to shape how you live.
Start with Ownership. Keep the whole Code.

Ownership gives you responsibility. Purpose gives it direction. Resilience protects that direction under pressure. Integrity keeps it honest. Discipline turns it into repeated action. Empowerment uses that strength to help others stand.
The teaching order follows the work of rebuilding, rather than the letters in PERIOD. You can open any lesson and return to it as life requires.
Ownership
Take responsibility for your response.
Purpose
Give responsibility a direction.
Resilience
Protect the direction under pressure.
Integrity
Bring conduct into alignment.
Discipline
Make the values repeatable.
Empowerment
Use your strength to build capability in others.
